title: Grocery Store Brand Deals for Creators: Retailer Pickup
summary: Grocery store brand deals for creators: what a pick-up-at-retailer campaign is, why location matters, filming in-store, receipts and getting booked.
body_markdown:
Grocery store brand deals for creators are one of the most practical campaign types in food. Instead of receiving a box at home, you go to a real store, find the product on the shelf, buy it, and show your followers exactly where to get it.


Our point of view: these campaigns reward being local, not being big. A creator whose followers live near the stores carrying a new product can be more useful to a brand than a larger account spread across the country.


## What is a grocery store brand deal for creators?


On Jupiter, this is called a Pick-up at Retailer campaign. Jupiter's


[creator page](https://www.jupiter.co/creators)


describes it simply: film the product in your own store.


A typical video follows the path a shopper would take:


1.


The store entrance or aisle, so followers know which chain carries it.


2.


The product on the shelf.


3.


The purchase.


4.


The product at home, going into a recipe. Our guide to


[sponsored recipe content that converts](https://www.jupiter.co/blog/how-to-create-sponsored-recipe-content-that-converts)


covers this part.


5.


The finished dish.


The value to the brand is the proof that the product is really there. Followers see the shelf, not just the packaging.


## Why do brands pay a premium near launch markets?


Jupiter says brands pay a premium for creators near launch markets. When a product has just been stocked in certain stores or regions, the people who can act on a video are the people who live near those shelves.


That's why your location is part of your pitch. Our guide to


[landing CPG brand deals as a food creator](https://www.jupiter.co/blog/how-to-land-cpg-brand-deals-food-creator)


covers how food brands choose creators more broadly.


## How do grocery store brand deals for creators work in practice?


Filming in a store comes with responsibilities a home shoot doesn't. A few habits keep it smooth:


-


**Ask first.**


Store policies differ, so check with a manager or staff member before you film.


-


**Keep it short.**


Get your shelf and checkout shots, then finish the rest at home.


-


**Protect other shoppers.**


Keep faces out of frame and never block an aisle.


-


**Shoot clean shelf shots.**


Tidy the facing of the product you're filming, but don't move competitors' products around.


-


**Go at quiet times.**


Early mornings and mid-afternoons on weekdays tend to be easier.


### Get considered for in-store campaigns


Jupiter runs brand campaigns for food creators, including Pick-up at Retailer campaigns.


## Proof of purchase and receipts


Campaigns like this often need proof that you bought the product where you said you did. Plan for it before you shop.


-


Keep the paper or digital receipt.


-


Film or photograph the product on the shelf and at checkout.


-


Note the store location and date.


Each campaign sets its own requirements, so read them first. Keep the receipt for your own records too, since campaign income and related costs belong in your bookkeeping.


## Disclosure


A paid in-store video is still a sponsored post. The FTC's


[Endorsement Guides](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-255/section-255.5)


call for clear disclosure of material connections, such as payment or free product. On YouTube, the


[paid product placement setting](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/154235)


adds a label for you.


## Getting booked on these campaigns


Brands pick creators for retailer campaigns on fit and location. Make both easy to see:


-


List your city or region in your


[food blogger media kit](https://www.jupiter.co/blog/how-to-create-a-food-blogger-media-kit)


and bio.


-


Mention the grocery chains you shop at regularly.


-


Show past posts where followers asked where to buy something.
